The process then tests structured problem solving directly through an online assessment and case interviews. No GPA cutoff is published on the official pages checked.

facts.claim: See London page candidate description and the ACI page requirements.

process_stages.description: Deadlines vary by school and office; US full-time had July 19, 2026 and October 11, 2026 deadlines in this cycle.
Numerical, logical reasoning and personality/behavioural components (described on the official London page; US assessment detail may vary by office).

interview_styles.style: Case interviews built on realistic client challenges, assessing how the candidate thinks and approaches problems, plus fit/leadership evidence from the resume
interview_styles.note: Bain's official interview-preparation material frames the consulting case as working through a realistic client problem. Community advice on how many practice cases to complete is folklore and is not quantified in this record.

thesis_text:
1. Bottom line: Bain's undergraduate door is the classic MBB shape - campus-led, deadline-driven, and decided by an online assessment plus case interviews - but it is officially open to every discipline. The practical filter is not your major; it is whether you hit an early dated deadline with a resume showing academics, leadership and quantified impact, and whether you can case at interview standard by fall.
2. Who gets in (sourced, qualitative): Undergraduates graduating December 2026-June 2027 for full-time (plus recent graduates within two years in the fall round) and December 2027-June 2028 for the intern role; all disciplines officially welcome.
3. Stated vs revealed screen: Stated: strong academics, analytical and communication skills, initiative, leadership and teamwork. Revealed: unknown from public data - no sourced cohort distribution exists in this record, so target-school share claims would be folklore.
4. Routes in, ranked: (1) Associate Consultant Intern converting to full-time, if you are a junior; (2) full-time Associate Consultant in the earliest deadline round you are prepared for; (3) an adjacent strategy or Big Four consulting role (see the Deloitte record) if the MBB window has closed for your graduation year.
5. Your gap: user-specific - compare school, experience, projects, skills and timing against the sourced signals in this record; no cohort percentages are claimed because no public population sample was available.
6. Plan: next 30 days - verify the live posting and deadline on the official page and build the role-specific skill evidence named in the posting; this semester - complete one internship, project or program that matches the entry route; this year - apply in the earliest window the firm offers for your graduation date.
7. Coffee-chat strategy: talk to recent entry-level hires and interns in the exact role family, and ask what the assessments and interviews actually tested and what surprised them.
8. Timeline and key dates: 2026 cycle: full-time July 19 and October 11, 2026 (the latter just passed as of this record); intern August 31, 2026. London Associate Consultant closes October 15, 2026 with interviews in November-early December. Re-verify the next US window on your school's official Bain page.
9. Risks and alternatives: The main risk is the calendar: missing a dated window costs a full cycle, and a July application blocks reapplying in the fall round. The hedge is applying the same case preparation to BCG, McKinsey and Deloitte windows, which sit close together.
10. Offer to execute: I can build the target list, tailor the resume to this record, and draft outreach - say the word.
known_biases_of_data: Deadline evidence mixes official Bain school pages with one university career center notice; the October date should be re-confirmed on an official page at application time.
Process detail (assessment vendor, two case rounds, November timing) is drawn from Bain's official London page and may differ in US offices.
No population data - stated eligibility (all disciplines) is not evidence about who is actually hired.
